hypothesis: Theorems CS-1 and CS-2 (paper papers/causal_semantics/paper.md) predict that for a message space M={m0,...,m5}, a context space C={c0,...,c3}, and the hand-built update operator Psi: M x C -> P(X) with X={x0,...,x3} of paper section 4, (a) the binary relation ~_Psi on M defined by 'Psi(m1, c) == Psi(m2, c) for every c in C' is a proper equivalence relation (reflexive, symmetric, transitive) on M; (b) its quotient M/~_Psi is exactly the four-class partition {{m0,m1},{m2,m3},{m4},{m5}}; (c) M/~_Psi is a common sufficient statistic (in the Theorem-4 sense) for the family {Psi(., c) : c in C} on M, meaning Psi(., c) is constant within each Psi-class for every c; and (d) the co-occurrence quotient M/~_kappa induced by the distractor signature kappa (even-indexed messages {m0,m2,m4} share signature (4,4,1,1); odd-indexed messages {m1,m3,m5} share signature (1,1,4,4)) is distinct from M/~_Psi -- neither partition refines the other and no cell coincides.

gates.CSP_CS1_PSI_EQUIVALENCE_IS_REFLEXIVE_SYM: The binary relation ~_Psi on M is verified reflexive, symmetric, and transitive by exhaustive enumeration of all 36 ordered pairs (reflexivity / symmetry) and all 216 ordered triples (transitivity).
gates.CSP_CS2_PSI_QUOTIENT_HAS_FOUR_CLASSES: The equivalence classes of ~_Psi on M are exactly {{m0,m1},{m2,m3},{m4},{m5}}.
gates.CSP_CS2_PSI_QUOTIENT_IS_COMMON_SUFFICIEN: For every context c in C, the downstream distribution Psi(., c) is constant within each Psi-class (within 1e-12 numerical tolerance).
gates.CSP_CS_COOCCURRENCE_PARTITION_DIFFERS_FR: The co-occurrence quotient M/~_kappa (two classes {{m0,m2,m4},{m1,m3,m5}}) and the Psi-quotient M/~_Psi (four classes {{m0,m1},{m2,m3},{m4},{m5}}) are distinct partitions of M.

compute.sampling: exact enumeration of the 6 x 4 Psi table and the 6-row co-occurrence matrix; no Monte Carlo.
